headline: CORN AT 52-WEEK HIGH; BEEF IMPORT SHOCK WEEK AHEAD
subheadline: Pro Farmer's below-consensus yield estimates hold corn near the top of its range heading into a week that will stress-test the cattle market.
lead: Corn finished Friday at $4.84, December at $5.08, both at or near 52-week highs and both carrying a yield story the funds actually believe. Pro Farmer's tour closed Aug 20 pointing below USDA's 180.7 bu/acre. Meanwhile, the cattle market is heading into a week defined by one announcement: Trump's 300,000 MT tariff-free beef import window, 90 days, live this week.
the_takeaway: Corn has the yield story; cattle has the import test. Know which one affects your operation most.
teaser: December corn at a 52-week high, a Pro Farmer yield cut underneath it, and a beef import window opening above the cattle market.

one_number.unit: inflation-adjusted Midwest farmland value decline, Q2 2026 year-over-year
one_number.context: The steepest real drop since 2016, per the Chicago Fed's Seventh District survey. Land is still nominally elevated, but when input costs and interest rates stay high and real values fall, the operating margin math gets harder before the next farm bill lands.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called corn down through $4.95. December corn closed Friday at $5.085, well above that level. Miss.
yesterdays_call.note: The Pro Farmer yield tour wrap gave funds a reason to stay long, not exit. The $4.95 target needed a demand-side crack that never materialized. No hedge credit here -- own it and watch the $5.00 floor instead.

sections.title: CORN HOLDS THE HIGH
sections.body:
- December corn held **$5.08** into Friday's close, at the top of its 52-week range, with Pro Farmer's tour wrap pointing below USDA's 180.7 bu/acre on corn yield, giving the funds a fundamental reason to stay long.
- Wheat at $6.82 gave back 4.75 cents on the session, diverging from corn, which tells you the buying is yield-story specific, not a broad grain lift.
- The week ahead has no WASDE and no Crop Progress on Monday, so Pro Farmer's number is the only fresh read until Thursday's export sales at 7:30 AM CT.
sections.catalyst: Pro Farmer crop tour closed Aug 20 pointing below USDA's 180.7 bu/acre corn yield estimate.
sections.bottom_line: Unpriced new-crop corn above $5.08 still has a window. Harvest pressure is coming.
sections.farmer_action: If you have unpriced new-crop corn and December holds above $5.00 Monday morning, that window is real and narrowing as combines approach. Price what you can defend before harvest basis pressure arrives.
sections.vs_yesterday: Corn: 52-week high held; tour yield story still the catalyst, not funds alone.

sections.title: CATTLE FACE THE IMPORT WEEK
sections.body:
- Live cattle settled at **$223.05** Friday, down fractionally, but the market is not yet fully pricing Trump's Aug 21 announcement of 300,000 MT tariff-free beef imports over 90 days, a policy that USDA Secretary Rollins has publicly backed.
- October live cattle closed $217.92 Thursday; if the import mechanics get clarified early in the week, that contract is the first pressure point to watch.
- The Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, has already removed roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity, so more imported beef into a processing-constrained market adds margin complexity, not just supply.
sections.catalyst: Trump's Aug 21 Truth Social post: 300,000 MT tariff-free beef imports over 90 days, with USDA Secretary Rollins endorsing the move.
sections.bottom_line: The 90-day import window is the week's cattle story. Watch October at $217.92 as the first support.
sections.farmer_action: Cattle feeders: hold major pricing decisions until the import volume mechanics and country-of-origin sourcing are clarified. A 90-day window against record-low placements is not permanent policy.
sections.vs_yesterday: Cattle: import shock confirmed by Rollins; October futures at $217.92 are the line to watch.

sections.title: BEANS FIRM, OIL SPLITS
sections.body:
- Soybeans finished at **$12.25** nearby and $12.39 November, up nearly 9-11 cents on the week, carried by China's purchase commitment (the May 18 deal, through 2028) and short covering into the close.
- Soybean meal added $2.00 to $317.70 while soybean oil dropped 2.1% to $69.35, the meal-oil divergence widening again as biodiesel demand expectations ease relative to crush demand for protein.
- If Pro Farmer's bean yield estimate runs below USDA's 52.7 bu/acre when the national figure surfaces, November beans have room to test higher; if it confirms USDA, the short covering is done.
sections.catalyst: China soybean purchase commitment ongoing since May 18; Pro Farmer tour national bean yield number in focus for directional resolution.
sections.bottom_line: Beans need a yield miss below 52.7 to sustain this move. The oil split is a margin story, not a demand story.

sections.title: WEEK AHEAD: WHAT TO WATCH
sections.body:
- Feeder cattle at **$334.75** enter the week with the Aug 24 Douglas, AZ port reopening for Mexican feeder imports now just one day out; the feeder/live spread is the tell on whether the market treats this as incremental or structural.
- El Nino moisture building across the central Plains through September adds a late-season crop development variable that the current corn and bean prices have not priced; watch the 6-10 day forecasts Monday morning.
- The Iran-Hormuz cycle, which re-escalated in July with commercial vessels hit and tankers reversing course before cooling into August, keeps WTI crude at $87.06 with the premium still deflating; diesel input costs for fall fieldwork remain the real farm-level concern.
sections.catalyst: Aug 24 phased feeder import reopening at Douglas AZ; El Nino autumn outlook issued by NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
sections.bottom_line: Three calendar events converge this week: import ports open, export sales print, and El Nino moisture forecasts sharpen.

outside_the_pit.title: Drought Forces Wyoming Ranchers to Cut Stocking Rates Now
outside_the_pit.body: Dry conditions across Wyoming are pushing ranchers to haul water and reduce herds earlier than planned. For producers elsewhere in the Northern Plains deciding whether to hold or sell stockers, this is forced selling that will show up in auction receipts before the Cattle on Feed count does.

outside_the_pit.title: Inflation-Adjusted Farmland Values Drop Most Since 2016
outside_the_pit.body: The Chicago Fed's Seventh District logged a 3.7% real decline in Q2 farmland values, the steepest since 2016. Nominal values still look high on paper, but if you are refinancing operating notes against land collateral this fall, the appraiser may be running a number you did not expect.

the_more_you_know.title: The Rhine Chokepoint That Is Not Making Ag Headlines
the_more_you_know.body: The Rhine River's Kaub gauge dropped below 10 cm in mid-August, its lowest on record. That gauge controls barge traffic into Germany's chemical and fertilizer production corridor. A sustained low forces rail and truck substitution at 3-4x the cost. European nitrogen production tightness this fall feeds into global urea prices by January, which feeds into your 2027 input bids. Watch it.

watch_list.desc: 6-10 day weather maps: El Nino moisture signals for central Plains matter for late soybean pod fill. Wetter-than-normal forecasts cap any remaining yield-cut premium.

Douglas AZ port reopens for Mexican feeder imports. If feeder futures open lower than $334.75 on Monday, the market is pricing the supply return. If they hold, the 90-day beef window is the bigger story.
Weekly export sales: corn above 500K MT confirms demand is holding the 52-week high; beans above 300K MT keeps the China-bid floor intact. Either one printing short flips the chart in charge.
Tariff-free beef import mechanism details: which countries, what cut specs, and whether USDA issues any country-of-origin guidance. Clarity here sets the cattle market's floor for the week.
